Title: Document 6
Content: Source: Hubert Reid, Jamaican veteran of a West Indian regiment in the British Army and leader of a labor union formed to defend the rights of Jamaican war veterans, petition to the British colonial government, `text(1935)`.

It has taken `17` `text(years)` of countless petitions, marching through the streets of Kingston,* as well as agitations before we were given worthless lands in some of the most remote parts of the island without even a well-needed `text(five-pound)` bill to assist us in making a shabby shelter, much less in trying to cultivate the place for an existence. In some cases, not even wild birds would care to inhabit the worthless lands that we were given. Not even an `text(inch)` is suitable for cultivation, and as far as roads are concerned, the inaccessibility of the places renders that impossible.
